cards.name: Overlapping Action
cards.what: Parts of an object move in the same direction with slightly offset start and stop times.
cards.conveys: Conveys weight and flexibility, making the object feel alive and natural.
useWhen: Move objects with connected parts, such as characters, icons, or groups of cards.
Let individual parts lag slightly as a list or group of cards moves together.

cards.name: Anticipation
cards.what: A brief movement in the opposite direction prepares the viewer for the main action.
cards.conveys: Signals the direction of travel and a buildup of force, making sudden motion easier to follow.
useWhen: Signal the launch direction of a character or icon.
Prepare the viewer's attention before a large movement.

sources.title: Twelve basic principles of animation, Anticipation

cards.name: Easing
cards.what: Easing changes velocity over the course of an animation while keeping its distance and duration constant.
cards.conveys: Adds weight to starts and stops; ease-out responds quickly and then settles smoothly.
useWhen: Compare the perceived speed of otherwise identical movements.
Make UI motion respond quickly and stop smoothly.

cards.name: Spring & Overshoot
cards.what: An object briefly exceeds its target scale before returning and settling.
cards.conveys: Shows inertia and restoring force as the object settles.
useWhen: Reveal a small object or settle it into a selected state.
Explain overshoot and recovery with a graph.

cards.name: Squash & Stretch
cards.what: An object stretches as it gains speed and squashes on impact while keeping the product of its axis scales constant.
cards.conveys: Conveys elasticity, weight, and the force of impact.
useWhen: Show the impact of a ball or flexible character.
Add elasticity to a small bounce.

sources.title: Twelve basic principles of animation, Squash and stretch

cards.name: Stagger
cards.what: Multiple elements appear in sequence with a consistent delay between them.
cards.conveys: Communicates element order and their relationship as a group.
useWhen: Show the reading order of a grid or list.
Spread out the entrance of multiple elements.

cards.name: Arcs
cards.what: An object follows a curved trajectory instead of a straight line.
cards.conveys: Conveys the natural flow of rotation and bouncing motion.
useWhen: Explain the trajectory of a bouncing or thrown ball.
Create more fluid movement through space than a straight-line translation.

sources.title: Twelve basic principles of animation, Arc

cards.name: Follow-through
cards.what: An attached extremity continues moving through inertia after the main body stops, then settles later.
cards.conveys: Conveys flexibility and inertia, showing that force remains after the main body stops.
useWhen: Show inertia in a flag or tail attached to a body.
Add weight and flexibility to an abrupt stop.

cards.name: Motion Hierarchy
cards.what: Differences in scale and entrance timing establish a reading order that prioritizes important information.
cards.conveys: Communicates an information hierarchy in which the title draws attention first, followed by the subtitle and details.
useWhen: Guide viewers through a title and its supporting information in stages.
Present information with different levels of importance on one screen.

cards.name: Timing & Spacing
cards.what: Spacing between successive frame positions reveals changes in velocity within the same movement duration.
cards.conveys: Shows that wider spacing means faster motion and tighter spacing means slower motion.
useWhen: Compare constant-speed and decelerating movement under identical conditions.
Explain easing-related velocity changes with motion trails.

cards.name: Motion Blending
cards.what: Two motions are mixed by weight so one action flows into the next.
cards.conveys: Poses connect without a jump, so the change feels continuous.
useWhen: When a character goes from walking to standing
When two poses must join without a popping frame

cards.name: Smear Frame
cards.what: During a fast move, the object stretches along its direction of travel and snaps back.
cards.conveys: Speed and impact. Frames read as connected rather than as a jump.
useWhen: When a swipe, swing or pop-out should hit in one or two frames
When a ball or icon crosses the screen with force

cards.name: Action Sequence
cards.what: One action finishes and the next begins, showing steps in order.
cards.conveys: The order of a process reads exactly. Viewers take one step at a time.
useWhen: When showing procedure or pipeline steps in order
When a cause is followed by its result

cards.name: Additive Motion
cards.what: A small wobble or rotation is layered on top of an element following a larger path.
cards.conveys: Makes elements read as one group and adds a subtle liveliness on top of the main motion.
useWhen: Give an icon or card weight by letting it sway while it travels.
Bind several elements to one parent rig so they move together.

cards.name: Beat Synchronization
cards.what: Arrivals, scale changes and cuts land exactly on specific beats of the music.
cards.conveys: Screen events and sound become one, giving rhythm and polish. Any drift from the beat feels wrong immediately.
useWhen: Cards or lines appear in sequence over music.
Time cuts to the beat to strengthen rhythm.

cards.name: Bounce Landing
cards.what: An object accelerates down, then bounces lower each time until it rests.
cards.conveys: Conveys gravity and impact, and gives the object weight and a ground plane.
useWhen: An icon or card drops from above and settles.
Announce arrival or completion with a lively touch.

cards.name: Concurrent Motion
cards.what: Several targets or properties move in the same window of time.
cards.conveys: Relationships between simultaneous changes. Things that change together are read at once.
useWhen: When two values move in opposite directions at the same time
When position and color change as one event

cards.name: Continuous Motion
cards.what: An element passes through several stops or scenes without pausing, keeping one flow.
cards.conveys: Separate steps read as one continuous action. Without stops, the expectation of direction holds.
useWhen: A marker passing stations A, B and C must run through without stopping.
Hand off velocity across a scene boundary.

cards.name: Group Motion
cards.what: Marks in one group move together in the same direction and speed so they read as a unit.
cards.conveys: Items that are far apart still read as one set when they move together (common fate).
useWhen: When showing which points belong to the same cluster in a scatter plot
When moving several cards as one category
When shifting dots by team or segment

cards.name: Inertial Glide
cards.what: A released object keeps its direction of travel and gradually decelerates to a stop.
cards.conveys: Conveys speed and friction, like something pushed and let go, with a natural stop.
useWhen: Let a card slide and stop after being pushed.
Let a list coast after a swipe.

cards.name: Motion Retargeting
cards.what: When the target changes mid-move, the element eases from its current position toward the new direction.
cards.conveys: Cancellations, reversals and data updates look smooth. The screen responds gracefully to a change of intent.
useWhen: Demonstrate an interaction where the destination changes mid-move.
Let live data updates continue from the current value instead of resetting.

cards.name: Rotation
cards.what: Turns an element around a center point to change its direction.
cards.conveys: Clearly tells that direction or posture has changed.
useWhen: When an arrow or expand icon turns with state
When rotating a card or diagram node 90 degrees to switch axis

cards.name: Scale
cards.what: Changes size proportionally from an anchor so growth direction and amount read clearly.
cards.conveys: Size change and where it unfolds from are told together.
useWhen: When a card or modal grows slightly as it appears
When a button dips and returns on press
When drawing bars that grow along one axis

cards.name: State Tween
cards.what: Position, size, rotation and color change together toward a saved next state.
cards.conveys: Shows one object's state changing continuously.
useWhen: When a card goes from collapsed to expanded
When an icon goes from idle to active
When a diagram node changes position and color together

cards.name: Stepped Motion
cards.what: Values or poses change instantly one step at a time without in-between interpolation.
cards.conveys: Carries the texture of digital steps and low frame rates. Against smooth animation it reads mechanical and crisp.
useWhen: Set a stop-motion or 8-bit brand tone.
Build counters or progress indicators that change in discrete steps.

cards.name: Temporal Overlap
cards.what: The next element starts moving before the first has stopped, so motion flows in a wave.
cards.conveys: Connected actions and fluid flow. Smoother than strict sequencing.
useWhen: When cards or icons enter in turn without a break
When one element's arrival should trigger the next in a chain

cards.name: Symmetric Panel Open
cards.what: Two panels enter from opposite sides and rotate toward a shared frontal plane.
cards.conveys: Gives two subjects equal visual weight for comparison.
useWhen: Compare two products with equally sized cards.
Reveal a before-and-after pair with synchronized timing.

cards.name: Back Entrance
cards.what: A small translucent element travels in, then settles at full size and opacity.
cards.conveys: Emphasizes arrival after a long movement.
useWhen: Bring a hero card in from a distance.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Blinds Reveal
cards.what: Staggered strips open to assemble a complete image.
cards.conveys: Creates a rhythm of separate pieces becoming a whole.
useWhen: Use when presenting blinds reveal in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Blur Reveal
cards.what: Blurred text or imagery resolves into sharp focus.
cards.conveys: Makes content feel as if it is emerging from mist.
useWhen: Use when presenting blur reveal in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Blurred Slide
cards.what: A stretched blurred element moves into place and resolves to its normal shape.
cards.conveys: Shows speed through a directional motion smear.
useWhen: Show a product moving rapidly.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Bomb Exit
cards.what: An element tilts sideways, moves away, and disappears into a heavy blur.
cards.conveys: Conveys an explosive departure or forceful removal.
useWhen: Show a game prop being forcefully removed.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Corner Mask Swing
cards.what: An opaque cover rotates around a corner to reveal content.
cards.conveys: Suggests lifting a lid or swinging a door aside.
useWhen: Use when presenting corner mask swing in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Counter Moving Matte
cards.what: A revealing window and its content move in opposite directions.
cards.conveys: Separates the boundary from the image for a dynamic reveal.
useWhen: Use when presenting counter moving matte in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Curtain Reveal
cards.what: Foreground objects part to reveal a title behind them.
cards.conveys: Reveals a hidden scene with depth.
useWhen: Use when presenting curtain reveal in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Depixelate Reveal
cards.what: Large pixel blocks resolve into a sharp image.
cards.conveys: Shows ambiguous imagery becoming concrete information.
useWhen: Use when presenting depixelate reveal in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Elliptic Entrance
cards.what: A tilted scaled element follows an elliptical-style path into a front-facing position.
cards.conveys: Suggests a three-dimensional travel path.
useWhen: Bring a card in along a curved path.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Fade Slide
cards.what: An element fades in while sliding into position.
cards.conveys: Makes the location and arrival order of new content clear.
useWhen: Use when presenting fade slide in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Fade
cards.what: An element appears or disappears through opacity alone.
cards.conveys: Creates a quiet beginning or ending.
useWhen: Reveal body text quietly.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Flicker Reveal
cards.what: An element switches on and off at uneven intervals before becoming fully visible.
cards.conveys: Suggests an electrical signal or an unstable connection.
useWhen: Represent a fictional signal connecting.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Flip Reveal
cards.what: An edge-on element rotates around a 3D axis to face the viewer.
cards.conveys: Suggests the front and back of a card or piece of information.
useWhen: Reveal new information on a card.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Foolish Reveal
cards.what: An element scales in while rotating around successive corner pivots.
cards.conveys: Creates a playful, unpredictable entrance.
useWhen: Introduce a comic character prop.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Hinge Drop
cards.what: An element swings from a corner, then drops out of view.
cards.conveys: Gives failure or removal a comic tone.
useWhen: Express a lighthearted game failure.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Hinge Reveal
cards.what: A panel rotates from its edge into a front-facing position.
cards.conveys: Makes concealed information feel like it is opening.
useWhen: Use when presenting hinge reveal in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Jack in the Box
cards.what: An element pops up from a tiny tilted state and settles through alternating rotations.
cards.conveys: Suggests a new arrival and surprise.
useWhen: Reveal a reward icon.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Light Speed
cards.what: An element rushes in sideways, skews, then straightens with a small counter-skew.
cards.conveys: Conveys speed and an abrupt arrival.
useWhen: Bring in a short breaking-news banner.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Magic Exit
cards.what: An element grows, rotates around an offset pivot, and leaves the frame.
cards.conveys: Creates a dramatic removal or scene ending.
useWhen: End a playful scene.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Mosaic Reveal
cards.what: Small tile windows reveal one complete image in sequence.
cards.conveys: Shows accumulated parts forming a whole.
useWhen: Use when presenting mosaic reveal in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Physical Exit
cards.what: An element accelerates off screen while rotating or falling.
cards.conveys: Gives an exit direction and physical weight.
useWhen: Use when presenting physical exit in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Puff Reveal
cards.what: An enlarged blurred element shrinks into focus, or expands and blurs away.
cards.conveys: Creates a soft appearance or disappearance.
useWhen: Reveal an image or logo softly.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Roll Reveal
cards.what: An element rolls in or out through sideways movement and planar rotation.
cards.conveys: Communicates playful movement and direction.
useWhen: Introduce a round icon playfully.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Rotate Reveal
cards.what: An element rotates in the plane while appearing or disappearing.
cards.conveys: Adds direction and energy to a reveal.
useWhen: Give a badge a directional reveal.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Scale Pop
cards.what: An element grows from a small scale to its final size.
cards.conveys: Clearly marks the arrival of a new element.
useWhen: Use when presenting scale pop in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

cards.name: Slide
cards.what: An element slides in from an edge or moves out of view.
cards.conveys: Makes the origin and direction of movement clear.
useWhen: Show where a side panel comes from.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Swap Entrance
cards.what: An oversized off-screen element sweeps around and shrinks into position.
cards.conveys: Signals an exaggerated replacement or surprise arrival.
useWhen: Replace the hero card with a new one.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Swirl Reveal
cards.what: An element spins through multiple turns while scaling into view.
cards.conveys: Creates a forceful, vortex-like entrance.
useWhen: Introduce a magic-effect icon.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Tilt Entrance
cards.what: An element arrives at an angle and removes its rotation and skew as it aligns.
cards.conveys: Makes energetic movement feel organized at the end.
useWhen: Align a tilted poster card.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

cards.name: Blur Resolve
cards.what: A blurred target sharpens as its blur radius falls, pulling the eye.
cards.conveys: The eye goes to what comes into focus. The blur to sharp direction leads attention.
useWhen: When a title or product shot arrives as if focusing
When the background stays soft and only the target sharpens

cards.name: Clip Reveal
cards.what: The visible region inside a boundary widens to reveal content from one side.
cards.conveys: Content opens along its edge and guides the reading direction.
useWhen: When a title or image opens upward like a shutter
When bars or lines are revealed with a direction

cards.name: Hard Appearance
cards.what: An element appears instantly at a defined moment.
cards.conveys: Makes a cut explicit and presents information immediately.
useWhen: Present information exactly on a cut.
Change state without an animated transition.

cards.name: Outline Flash Reveal
cards.what: A bright outline traces the subject while its interior fades into clarity.
cards.conveys: Combines an entrance with a focused attention cue.
useWhen: Draw attention to an entering icon.
Explain the relationship between outline and fill.

cards.name: Paper Shred Exit
cards.what: A document feeds through a slit and falls away as narrow strips.
cards.conveys: Communicates destruction and a completed deletion.
useWhen: Visualize a confirmed deletion.
Explain how a document is dismantled.

cards.name: Spiral Assembly
cards.what: Pieces spiral inward and settle into their final arrangement.
cards.conveys: Communicates convergence and assembly.
useWhen: Assemble scattered pieces.
Show separate parts becoming a single structure.

cards.name: Letter Spin In
cards.what: Letters arrive tilted or spinning and rotate into their upright alignment.
cards.conveys: A light, playful title rhythm with a little life in every character.
useWhen: Bright, light-toned titles and intros
Titles for kids, education or commerce shorts

cards.name: Overwhelm Surround
cards.what: Cards arrive increasingly quickly around a stationary focal subject.
cards.conveys: Builds a sense of overload and spatial pressure.
useWhen: Introduce a workload problem.
Build pressure before presenting a solution.

cards.name: Threshold Pulse
cards.what: A counter becomes more prominent and briefly scales up when it reaches a warning threshold.
cards.conveys: Signals limited remaining capacity or an approaching limit.
useWhen: Warn when remaining storage falls below 20 percent.
Emphasize a countdown entering its final warning range.

cards.name: Border Reveal
cards.what: A border line closes in from outside the element to reveal its outline.
cards.conveys: Marks a selected element or an important boundary without filling it.
useWhen: When a form field or card becomes selected
When pointing at the edge of an on-screen element

cards.name: Jello
cards.what: A damped alternating shear that makes an element wobble like jelly.
cards.conveys: A soft, squishy material that responds elastically when touched.
useWhen: When a jelly-like character or soft UI card is pressed
In app intro videos with a playful brand tone

cards.name: Pulse
cards.what: A short scale beat where an element grows slightly and returns to its size in place.
cards.conveys: Signals the element is alive and clickable. It draws the eye without moving anything.
useWhen: When pulling attention to a button or badge that should be pressed now
When showing an active state such as a notification dot or record indicator
When pointing at one icon during an explanation

cards.name: Rotate Scale
cards.what: An element spins while growing, then settles back to its original size.
cards.conveys: Adds energy to one object's entrance or state change.
useWhen: When a logo or icon should land with force
When showing a state change such as unlock or done with an icon

cards.name: Tada
cards.what: A celebratory shrink-then-grow with a small left-right shake before settling.
cards.conveys: Announces an achievement or completion. It is short and cheerful and ends cleanly.
useWhen: When signalling a goal reached, a payment done or an upload finished
When stressing a badge or trophy icon right after it appears

cards.name: Wobble
cards.what: A wide left-right sway with tilt that shrinks in amplitude until it settles.
cards.conveys: Reads as instability, playfulness or a soft rejection. Decay to rest is the key.
useWhen: When a cute character or sticker reacts
When a bad input should bounce back lightly
When adding a playful emphasis in short-form video

cards.name: Audio Reactive Pulse
cards.what: Shape size and glow intensity follow the low or high frequency strength of the sound.
cards.conveys: Music and picture feel like one event, making sound visible.
useWhen: Need sound-reactive elements in a music video or logo intro.
Let a background glow breathe with the music.

cards.name: Blink
cards.what: An element's brightness or opacity switches on and off repeatedly.
cards.conveys: Signals warning, presence or in-progress state. It is the simplest attention cue.
useWhen: Use on small indicators such as recording, live or warnings.
Show a cursor or input position.

cards.name: Bounce Attention
cards.what: An element bounces up and down in place, then returns to its original position.
cards.conveys: Creates liveliness and draws attention to a selectable target. It also works as a cue to click.
useWhen: Nudge people to press a button or notification icon.
Announce a newly added list item.

cards.name: Circumscribe
cards.what: A circle or rectangle is drawn around a target and then erased.
cards.conveys: Makes the extent of what is being explained clear, then steps back.
useWhen: When briefly circling a formula, code piece or chart region
When picking one item out of several on screen

cards.name: Color Transition
cards.what: An element's color blends smoothly from its current color to the next.
cards.conveys: Signals activation, a role change or a state transition.
useWhen: When a button or node goes from idle to active
When a chart bar crosses a threshold and turns to a warning color

cards.name: Focus Contraction
cards.what: A wide, translucent disk shrinks onto the target and vanishes.
cards.conveys: A sighting cue that says look here. Attention converges from outside in.
useWhen: When a small button or number must be pinpointed
When pulling the eye to the target after a long screen change

cards.name: Focus Handoff
cards.what: Among items already laid out, one lights up at a time and the highlight hands off to the next.
cards.conveys: Viewers see which item is being explained and the reading order at a glance.
useWhen: Explain four items in turn and light only the current one.
Build a list scene synced with narration.

cards.name: Outline Pulse
cards.what: A shape's edge line appears and briefly thickens and brightens before easing back.
cards.conveys: Reveals the selected form clearly on a busy screen.
useWhen: When tracing the outline of a product or person in a photo
When marking a 3D object or icon as selected

cards.name: Radial Speed Lines
cards.what: Lines from the center burst outward briefly and vanish.
cards.conveys: Delivers impact and rapid expansion in one moment. Like manga focus lines, it gathers the eye at the center.
useWhen: Emphasize the instant a key word or product slams onto the screen.
Pull attention to the center right after a cut.

cards.name: Selection Travel
cards.what: A translucent selection band moves from one range to the next, resizing to fit.
cards.conveys: Reads the grammatical range of what is being explained. One band moving keeps continuity.
useWhen: When walking through code lines or tokens one by one
When a chart's period range is moved along section by section

cards.name: Shake
cards.what: An element oscillates on both sides of its rest position or angle, then stops.
cards.conveys: Draws attention or signals refusal, instability or error. A local eye-catching cue for small elements.
useWhen: Shake a form field to signal an input error.
Get a notification icon noticed.

cards.name: Swing
cards.what: An element hung from a fixed pivot rotates side to side, shrinking in amplitude until it rests.
cards.conveys: Gives cards a hanging, force-driven physicality. Pendulum damping produces a natural stop.
useWhen: A hanging card or sign settles with a gentle sway after entering.
Signal a notification or change with a swing.

cards.name: Vignette Pulse
cards.what: The dark edge of the frame tightens inward for an instant and then releases.
cards.conveys: Conveys the pressure of impact or a decisive moment, with a brief tension that focuses the eye on the center.
useWhen: Focus attention on the center at an impact or key announcement.
Express tension at the end of a countdown.

cards.name: Text Color Wipe
cards.what: Bright text fills over dim text from one side.
cards.conveys: Communicates reading position and progress at once; the phrase itself becomes the progress indicator.
useWhen: Show a loading or progress phrase as a letter fill.
Read a long sentence along with scrolling.

cards.name: Letter Drop Pile
cards.what: The letters of a sentence detach, fall, hit the ground, and pile up.
cards.conveys: Shows a phrase breaking apart with weight, and leaves a heap of letters as the result.
useWhen: Back up a phrase that means collapse or spill with a visual.
Break text apart in an error or failure scene.

cards.name: Per-character Rise
cards.what: Characters rise from below and fade in with a staggered delay.
cards.conveys: Communicates the reading direction and sequential entrance of a title.
useWhen: Reveal a short title in reading order.
Add rhythm to a sentence's entrance.

cards.name: Highlight Sweep
cards.what: A highlighter band sweeps from left to right behind a key phrase.
cards.conveys: Clearly identifies the phrase that deserves attention within a sentence.
useWhen: Call out a key phrase in a sentence.
Emphasize the meaning of a sentence that has already been read.

cards.name: Kinetic Beats
cards.what: Words hit the center at a large scale on regular beats and quickly settle.
cards.conveys: Communicates a three-step rhythm and emphasizes the final action.
useWhen: Compress a sequence into short verbs.
Focus attention on the final key action.

cards.name: Mask Reveal
cards.what: A title rises into clipped windows to reveal one line at a time.
cards.conveys: Introduces a title through a sequential reveal of its lines.
useWhen: Introduce a two-line title in sequence.
Focus attention on the start of a paragraph.

cards.name: Text Scramble
cards.what: Symbols cycle in each character position before resolving into the final text from left to right.
cards.conveys: Shows an uncertain sequence of characters converging into a readable sentence.
useWhen: Give a short title a decoding effect.
Reveal an answer or result as it becomes progressively resolved.

cards.name: Typewriter
cards.what: A sentence appears one character at a time at regular intervals while a cursor follows the insertion point.
cards.conveys: Communicates the process of writing and sequential text input.
useWhen: Show a short input sentence being composed.
Show a typing state in a conversational UI.

cards.name: Underline Draw
cards.what: An SVG path draws beneath a key phrase from left to right in a single stroke.
cards.conveys: Emphasizes the words to read as if pointing to them by hand.
useWhen: Call attention to a key phrase once.
Add a handwritten emphasis to a sentence.

cards.name: Word Emphasis
cards.what: A phrase changes color and scale within a stationary sentence while surrounding text fades.
cards.conveys: Communicates the key phrase to read and the priority of information.
useWhen: Focus attention on a key phrase within a sentence.
Align visual focus with an emphasized moment in narration.

cards.name: Kinetic Type Sweep
cards.what: Three lines of 200px+ serif type sweep across the frame in opposite directions at different speeds, then one key word slams to a stop dead center.
cards.conveys: Many words stream past and one gets chosen. The speed of the flow gives the stop its weight.
useWhen: Stamp a single theme word in the first three seconds of a video.
Show one choice being picked from many candidates with type alone.
Introduce a large section title at a transition.

cards.name: Context Caret
cards.what: A text caret that changes color with the kind of text being typed, then keeps blinking.
cards.conveys: The caret alone tells the viewer which segment is active, so the input feels alive.
useWhen: When typing text whose segments carry different meaning, such as a brand word or a verification result
When an AI answer streams and you want to quietly mark the active segment

cards.name: 3D Flip Decode
cards.what: Each character rotates through a few random symbols and lands on its true glyph.
cards.conveys: A mechanical decoding progression, with the moment of certainty clearly visible.
useWhen: A title that reveals a security, decoding or analysis result
A scene where an AI locks in its reasoning result

cards.name: Font Shuffle
cards.what: The sentence stays put while a key word changes typeface on every beat.
cards.conveys: Shows one word taking on different personalities in time with the music; the font change acts as a rhythm instrument.
useWhen: Give a keyword a different face on each beat in a music video.
Sweep a brand-value word through several typefaces.

cards.name: Glyph Roll
cards.what: Each character sits in a vertical slot that rolls until the next glyph lands.
cards.conveys: Information updates with mechanical precision, like a counter or a booking board.
useWhen: When a button label or status word changes to another value
When a short code, number or status word refreshes

cards.name: Handwriting Write On
cards.what: A pen tip travels along the real stroke order so the handwriting is revealed.
cards.conveys: The hand and pace of a person writing: personal and careful.
useWhen: Signatures, greetings and handwritten titles
Emotionally emphasizing a small word

cards.name: Inline Image Expand
cards.what: A small inline image between words grows and pushes the surrounding text aside.
cards.conveys: The subject the sentence described takes over the frame, moving naturally from text to picture inside the line.
useWhen: Enlarge the subject in a sentence like 'We make [image]'.
Move from a text scene to a photo scene.

cards.name: Letter Anagram Shift
cards.what: The letters of one word travel to become the initials of a new word or list.
cards.conveys: Shows the same material reconnecting into a new structure; letters move instead of vanishing, which keeps continuity.
useWhen: Move from a word to a list where each letter becomes an item initial.
Break a menu title into individual item labels.

cards.name: Phrase Push Build
cards.what: Each new word enters from the right and pushes earlier words left, keeping the whole phrase centered.
cards.conveys: The sentence grows while the eye stays on one center point, matching spoken rhythm.
useWhen: When building a short slogan word by word into a finished sentence
When showing one line of narration as rhythmic typography

cards.name: Quote Card Build
cards.what: The quotation mark and lines appear in order and the attribution attaches last.
cards.conveys: Makes the relation between statement and speaker clear and gives time to read; the weight of a quote comes from the order.
useWhen: Show a single review or interview line as a card.
Quote a speaker on a slide.

cards.name: Repeated Text Wall
cards.what: One phrase is duplicated into many rows that fill the screen.
cards.conveys: Builds presence and the overwhelming feel of repetition into a rhythmic screen texture.
useWhen: Extend a brand name or campaign line into a background pattern.
End a title by flooding the frame with the phrase.

cards.name: Scene Integrated Title
cards.what: The title is revealed and hidden in step with lines or character paths inside the scene.
cards.conveys: Places the title inside the story world so it reads as part of the scene rather than a caption.
useWhen: Let a title pass behind an object in an opening.
Align letters with lines such as columns or buildings as they appear.

cards.name: Spatial Word Composition
cards.what: Words appear in spoken order, changing size and angle to fill the frame as one typographic composition.
cards.conveys: Emphasis and meaning relations are carried by placement; speech rhythm becomes a picture.
useWhen: Turning a narration paragraph into a keyword-led type poster
Expressing an emotional sentence through big and small type

cards.name: Split Flap Display
cards.what: The top and bottom halves of each character card flip along a hinge to form a new glyph.
cards.conveys: Mechanical, sequential information updates, like an airport board, made tangible.
useWhen: Short tabular info that updates, such as times, rankings or stock counts
A retro mechanical counter or title

cards.name: Strikethrough Replace
cards.what: A strikethrough is drawn over the old text, then the new text appears beside or below it.
cards.conveys: It shows that a claim was withdrawn and replaced, through order alone.
useWhen: When showing a changed price, figure or policy next to its previous value
When striking down a myth and putting the correct claim in its place

cards.name: Text Scatter Assemble
cards.what: Letters scattered around the frame fly in and settle into a readable sentence.
cards.conveys: Shows scattered information being organized into meaning, with attention converging just before arrival.
useWhen: Open a title while also conveying that pieces come together.
Start a cinematic opening title.

cards.name: Text Wave
cards.what: A narrow wave sweeps a sentence and lifts only the glyphs it passes.
cards.conveys: The eye follows reading direction and rhythm, and the sentence seems to breathe.
useWhen: Lightly animating a loading or idle line
Bouncing a title on the beat in music-driven video

cards.name: Text Window Fill
cards.what: The letter outlines stay fixed while video or color flows only inside them.
cards.conveys: Ties the words to the visual subject so a single large title sets the mood of the scene.
useWhen: Let an intro title carry its own subject footage, such as sea or city.
Add a moving texture to a logo or a one-word slogan.

cards.name: Tracking Reveal
cards.what: Widely spaced letters tighten together until the title settles into one compact unit.
cards.conveys: Refined cohesion: scattered elements aligning to signal trust and calm.
useWhen: Title reveals in luxury or brand films
Settling a section name or subtitle quietly

cards.name: Variable Font Axis Morph
cards.what: A word's weight and width change continuously, shifting its intensity and character.
cards.conveys: The same word moves from a light voice to a solid one, gaining weight.
useWhen: When a key word should grow from thin to bold for emphasis
When text personality should change on hover or selection

cards.name: Variable Font Weight Wave
cards.what: A wave of weight and slant passes through the letters of a variable font.
cards.conveys: The type itself feels alive and rhythmic, carrying brand tone without a logo.
useWhen: When adding life to a variable-font brand headline
When a loading or idle screen needs motion from text alone

cards.name: Word Relay
cards.what: One big word enters from the right, pauses at center, exits left, and the next word takes over.
cards.conveys: The message is passed along word by word like a baton, and the last word stays as the conclusion.
useWhen: When showing a 2 to 5 word slogan one huge word at a time
When delivering keywords in sequence within one scroll section

cards.name: Word Rise Fade
cards.what: Words rise slightly while shedding blur, settling into place one after another.
cards.conveys: A calm, orderly sentence build where reading order is visible as word order.
useWhen: When revealing a one or two line explainer caption or subtitle softly
For the calm brand-tone opening line of a video

cards.name: Word Slot Cycle
cards.what: The fixed part of a sentence stays put while one word slot cycles through alternatives.
cards.conveys: One sentence frame carries many options, signalling range and variety.
useWhen: When showing many uses in one frame, such as "Build ___ with AI"
When a product headline rotates through audiences or features

cards.name: Crossfade
cards.what: Scene A fades out as scene B fades in at the same time.
cards.conveys: Briefly lets both scenes coexist, connecting the sentence to probability information.
useWhen: Move smoothly from a sentence to a related data scene.
Connect two scenes that share a continuous sense of time or atmosphere.

cards.name: Push
cards.what: An incoming scene pushes the existing scene out by the same amount in the same direction.
cards.conveys: Makes two scenes feel like adjoining spaces.
useWhen: Move between ordered steps.
Show the spatial relationship when moving to an adjacent scene.

cards.name: Wipe
cards.what: A moving boundary progressively reveals the new scene behind it.
cards.conveys: Communicates the entrance of a new scene through a boundary moving in a consistent direction.
useWhen: Present information in order from left to right.
Replace the entire scene while keeping the transition boundary visible.

cards.name: Shape Mask Transition
cards.what: A circular mask expands from a point to reveal the next scene.
cards.conveys: Shows new information spreading across the screen from a shared origin.
useWhen: Transition from a question to its answer.
Open a detail scene from a selected point.

cards.name: Match Cut
cards.what: Matching shapes at the same position and size connect two scenes across a cut.
cards.conveys: Connects a sentence to data by matching its final period to a chart dot.
useWhen: Connect different scenes through objects with matching shapes.
Keep the viewer's gaze in place when moving from explanation to data.

cards.name: Morph
cards.what: The same element changes shape and color to become a component of the next scene.
cards.conveys: Maintains the connection between information and the continuity of an object as its shape changes.
useWhen: Transform an input shape into a bar in output data.
Carry the same object across scenes in a different role.

cards.name: Whip Pan
cards.what: A rapid horizontal sweep with horizontal blur and sharp deceleration settles into the next scene.
cards.conveys: Moves attention to the next information as if the camera rapidly pans.
useWhen: Move quickly from a question to a result.
Maintain speed and direction across consecutive scenes.

cards.name: Zoom Through
cards.what: The opening in the letter O enlarges to carry the viewer through to the next scene inside it.
cards.conveys: Connects to the next information by moving deeper toward a shared center.
useWhen: Use the inside of a title letter as an entrance to the next scene.
Move from an overview into details such as probabilities.

cards.name: Blur Dissolve
cards.what: Two scenes overlap while blurred, swap, and the new scene sharpens back into focus.
cards.conveys: A soft shift in time or mood, as if focus is moving instead of the picture being cut.
useWhen: Bridge a time skip or location change smoothly.
Join two shots of a similar tone without a hard cut.

cards.name: Bounce Transition
cards.what: The scene boundary drops, bounces off the floor several times with a trailing shadow, and reveals the new scene.
cards.conveys: Makes a scene feel like a physical object with weight. Light and cheerful.
useWhen: When dropping a scene in to cover the old one in a casual, bright explainer
When a product card bounces in from below to open the next section

cards.name: Burn Transition
cards.what: An irregular edge burns outward, erasing the old scene and revealing the next, leaving a hot glow along the border.
cards.conveys: Destruction and a fresh start, given dramatic weight by the glowing edge.
useWhen: Mark the turning point from an old way to a new one in a story.
Open or climax a piece that needs a tactile, dramatic texture.

cards.name: Chromatic Wipe
cards.what: Color channels split apart as the frame slides away, then recombine on the new frame.
cards.conveys: Digital speed and lens distortion: a cold, technical impression.
useWhen: Move quickly between scenes in a tech or cyber-toned video.
Add an extra layer of texture on top of a wipe.

cards.name: Clock Wipe
cards.what: A rotating pie-shaped edge sweeps from the center and reveals the next scene.
cards.conveys: The feeling of time passing, as if a clock hand is opening the next scene.
useWhen: Move into a scene about timelines, progress, or elapsed time.
Change scenes with a single rhythmic sweep.

cards.name: Column Melt
cards.what: A scene is cut into vertical strips that drop at different speeds, revealing the next scene like a melting screen.
cards.conveys: The old screen collapses under its own weight. Rough, playful, and clearly game-like.
useWhen: When erasing a scene with a retro, game, or comedic tone
When one cut in a short-form clip needs to stand out

cards.name: Cube Transition
cards.what: Two scenes rotate in perspective like neighboring faces of a cube, with a hint of floor reflection.
cards.conveys: Makes both scenes feel attached to one 3D object. Suggests space rotating.
useWhen: When showing tabs or sections as adjacent faces and moving to the next one
When going from a feature A screen to a feature B screen in a product tour

cards.name: Dip to Color
cards.what: The outgoing scene fades into a flat color, then the next scene rises out of that same color.
cards.conveys: A section or chapter break: a pause before the next idea.
useWhen: Mark clearly where a chapter or section changes.
Cut between two mismatched scenes through a single color field.

cards.name: Flash Transition
cards.what: A white flash covers the frame, the scene changes at the peak, and brightness recovers.
cards.conveys: Impact and a hard beat: the cut on the downbeat is burned into the eye.
useWhen: Change scenes on a music beat or emphasized line.
Gather attention just before a product reveal or title.

cards.name: Halftone Dissolve
cards.what: Circular holes on a grid grow and merge to reveal the next scene.
cards.conveys: A print and stipple texture: a retro, graphic swap.
useWhen: Change scenes in a retro, print, or pop-art styled video.
Reveal radially from a starting point.

cards.name: Page Turn
cards.what: A page corner curls up, exposing the back and a soft shadow, and turns to the next screen.
cards.conveys: Evokes turning to the next page of a story. Signals order and progress gently.
useWhen: When splitting tutorial steps or story chapters like turning pages
When the subject is paper media such as ebooks, manuals, or albums

cards.name: Perspective Swap
cards.what: Two scenes swap left-right and front-back like perspective cards, with reflections following.
cards.conveys: Signals a change in who leads. Makes before-and-after or priority handoffs readable.
useWhen: When showing the moment two screens trade roles, such as old and new versions
When two cards trade places to indicate a rank or priority change

cards.name: Ripple Dissolve
cards.what: Concentric ripples spread from one point, bending the frame while revealing the next scene.
cards.conveys: An organic wobble like a stone dropped in water: the scene changes as if it were liquid.
useWhen: Give a scene change a soft, physical quality.
Trigger the change from a click or touch point in UI demos.

cards.name: Rotating Tile Dissolve
cards.what: Tiled copies of the frame rotate around the origin while the next scene blends in.
cards.conveys: Adds rotation and a flowing pattern that crosses the frame edge.
useWhen: When blending scenes in a pattern-driven, graphic-heavy video
On beat-driven short-form cuts where the frame spins into the next shot

cards.name: Scale Swap
cards.what: The old element shrinks toward a pivot while the new one grows in to take its place.
cards.conveys: Different states continue in the same spot, with a small pop.
useWhen: Change an icon, card, or button into another state.
Swap one scene for another in the same position.

cards.name: Split Slide
cards.what: Two halves of the frame slide apart or together in opposite directions and swap scenes.
cards.conveys: Gives openings and closings a clear, symmetric rhythm.
useWhen: When opening a new screen like doors at a section start
When swapping a symmetric layout with a tidy, orderly feel

cards.name: Squeeze Transition
cards.what: The outgoing scene is squashed along one axis while the next scene unfolds from the same edge.
cards.conveys: Space is exchanged by compression and expansion, like a door closing and reopening.
useWhen: Emphasize a big left-right or up-down state change.
Swap one card or panel for different content.

cards.name: Stereo Viewer Swap
cards.what: The scene shrinks into a rounded window, two copies rotate apart, and after a dark gap the new scene opens and zooms back up.
cards.conveys: Gives a physical swap feel, like slides in a viewer.
useWhen: When flipping between two screens like a viewer window in a product tour
For catalog or photo-album subjects where items are viewed one at a time

cards.name: Tangent Motion Blur Spin
cards.what: The scene spins around a corner and smears along the tangent of its path as it is replaced.
cards.conveys: Conveys speed and inertia of rotation strongly.
useWhen: For energetic openings or highlight cuts that need a sense of speed
For trailer-style transitions where the frame whips around into the next scene

cards.name: Additive Dissolve
cards.what: The bright colors of two scenes add together, brightening the middle before settling to the next scene.
cards.conveys: Adds light and liveliness to a scene change.
useWhen: To ease a light, airy scene change such as a memory, dream, or intro
To carry a product video from one screen to the next like spreading light

cards.name: Band Slide
cards.what: Video bands split horizontally or vertically slide at slightly different timings to reveal the next screen.
cards.conveys: Gives a line-by-line rhythm to the whole frame.
useWhen: When switching a list, table, or row-structured screen line by line
To create a tidy rhythm in presentation section transitions

cards.name: Channel Phase Dissolve
cards.what: Red, green, and blue channels hand over to the new scene at different times.
cards.conveys: A swap that exposes digital processing: channels fall out of step and color bleeds.
useWhen: Add character to a crossfade in a technical, digital-toned video.
Get a gentler color-split effect than a glitch.

cards.name: Chapter Interstitial
cards.what: A step-title card appears between scenes, holds briefly, then hands off to the next scene.
cards.conveys: Makes the boundaries of long demos or explanations clear.
useWhen: To split a long demo or tutorial into step 1, step 2, and so on
At chapter changes to show where the viewer is

cards.name: Clone Wall Wipe
cards.what: A wall of tiles repeating the same word fills the frame, inverts, then clears.
cards.conveys: A hard boundary that hammers a message by repetition: typography-led style.
useWhen: Leave a key word behind strongly as scenes change.
Use in type-driven openers or chapter cards.

cards.name: Color Distance Dissolve
cards.what: Areas where the two scenes differ most in color swap at different speeds from areas where they match.
cards.conveys: The picture's own content decides the order of the change: similar colors melt across first.
useWhen: Connect two scenes with the same layout but different colors, such as before and after.
Want a dissolve whose grain is set by the content itself.

cards.name: Cross Cutting
cards.what: Scenes from two places or actions are shown alternately.
cards.conveys: Helps viewers grasp simultaneous progress, comparison, or tension.
useWhen: When showing two parallel efforts at once, such as development and marketing
When building tension toward a moment where two lines meet, like a chase or deadline countdown

cards.name: Cutaway
cards.what: The main action is interrupted by a brief related shot or reaction, then it returns.
cards.conveys: Fills in context and naturally hides edit gaps.
useWhen: When briefly showing a related screen or reference during an explanation
When covering a slip of the tongue or an edit jump with another shot

cards.name: Datamosh Transition
cards.what: Horizontal strips and vertical slits tear, old footage residue smears, and the next screen takes over.
cards.conveys: Produces the friction and destruction of corrupted compressed video.
useWhen: In music videos, games, and experimental pieces when tearing between scenes
On a shocking reversal cut that needs a collapsing feel

cards.name: Edge Trace Stylization
cards.what: The photo's surfaces vanish, leaving only edges as a line drawing.
cards.conveys: From photo to structure. The skeleton of the form is exposed, giving a diagrammatic, analytical impression.
useWhen: Move from a product photo to a structural explanation.
Turn a realistic image into a blueprint or sketch look.

cards.name: Exit Before Enter
cards.what: The previous element fully disappears before the new one appears.
cards.conveys: A clear, sequential change of state, with no overlap to muddy the read.
useWhen: Change the content of a card, line of text, or tab in the same spot.
Replace text where overlapping elements would be hard to read.

cards.name: Eyeline Match
cards.what: After a person looks off-screen, the object in that direction appears.
cards.conveys: Lets viewers understand who is looking at what.
useWhen: When a person looks off-screen and the shot moves to what they saw
When a user looks up and the alert or menu at the top of the screen is shown next

cards.name: Fly Eye Transition
cards.what: The frame breaks into tiny lenses that magnify and refract, split colors, and cross into the next scene.
cards.conveys: An unfamiliar view like a compound eye or glass surface: refraction as through a prism.
useWhen: Give an experimental, technical video a distinctive transition.
Themes such as glass, lenses, or insects.

cards.name: Frame Border Transition
cards.what: A thick frame or border moves or grows to hide the cut and enclose the new screen.
cards.conveys: Makes viewers feel scenes change inside a branded frame.
useWhen: When a brand-colored frame fills the screen and opens onto the next scene
To unify corner transitions in a series with one frame motif

cards.name: Freeze Cut
cards.what: A moment of action freezes and holds briefly before the scene changes.
cards.conveys: Emphasizes a key moment or the end of a paragraph.
useWhen: To freeze on a result moment (a goal, completion, success) and add a caption
To end a section on a freeze frame that signals the paragraph is done

cards.name: Freeze Frame Dressing
cards.what: Motion freezes on the beat and paper, tape, and labels stick around the frozen subject.
cards.conveys: A marker that says this moment matters: a magazine cover or documentary intro shot.
useWhen: Introduce a person or product for the first time.
Make a decisive moment memorable.

cards.name: Glitch Transition
cards.what: Video blocks momentarily misalign and color channels or ghosts break apart while the scene is replaced.
cards.conveys: Creates a signal-error look and a rough transition shock.
useWhen: When cutting roughly between scenes in a tech, cyber, or hacking tone
To grab attention on the first cut of a short-form opener

cards.name: Gravitational Lens Transition
cards.what: The frame bends around the center, light gathers into a ring, and it resolves into the new frame.
cards.conveys: A sense of enormous force warping space: a weighty, sci-fi style move.
useWhen: Change chapters in a video about space, physics, or technological scale.
Open strongly by pulling attention to one point.

cards.name: Grayscale Dissolve
cards.what: Saturation drains from both scenes mid-transition, they blend in black and white, then color returns on the new scene.
cards.conveys: Memory and recollection: color leaves and returns as time shifts.
useWhen: Hint at a flashback or change of viewpoint.
Bridge two color scenes whose palettes clash in a crossfade.

cards.name: Grid Flip
cards.what: Rectangular tiles cut from the scene flip in sequence to reveal the next scene on their backs.
cards.conveys: A flow where partial changes accumulate into a full one: cards flip one after another.
useWhen: Change the whole state of a dashboard or card UI.
Swap scenes in a wave-like tile order.

cards.name: Hard Cut
cards.what: Switches straight to the next picture with no overlap.
cards.conveys: Marks the start of a new scene and a meaning boundary at once. It cuts rhythm to open a new topic.
useWhen: When the topic changes and the break should be clear
When cutting scenes quickly on the beat
When a surprise or contrast is wanted

cards.name: Held Scene Overlap
cards.what: While the next scene starts, the previous scene's motion is held briefly, and the new scene is revealed at the end of the delay.
cards.conveys: Lets the end of an action and the scene change be timed independently.
useWhen: When the next scene starts before the previous scene's final motion has finished
When dialogue or sound belongs to the next scene but the picture should linger

cards.name: HSV Dissolve
cards.what: Hue travels along the color wheel while scenes mix, with saturation and brightness shifting together.
cards.conveys: Color change is felt before realistic blending: a rainbow-tinted move between scenes.
useWhen: Brand videos or music visuals where color itself is the story.
When you want a showy pixel-level cross blend.

cards.name: Insert Shot
cards.what: A close-up of a hand or object briefly cuts in between wide action.
cards.conveys: Makes an important clue in the action unmistakable.
useWhen: To magnify a small button or screen area during a product operation
To supplement a material or tool detail during cooking or process footage

cards.name: Jump Cut
cards.what: The person or state jumps instantly within the same framing.
cards.conveys: Compresses time and conveys deliberate discontinuity.
useWhen: To remove pauses and dead time from a talking head or screen recording in a fixed position
For long processes like builds or coding that need compressing

cards.name: Kaleidoscope Transition
cards.what: The picture folds into symmetric fragments, rotates, blends into the next scene, and unfolds back to a normal frame.
cards.conveys: A colorful, fantastical pattern move, like turning a kaleidoscope.
useWhen: Music visuals, festivals, or dreamy-toned videos.
When an eye-catching decorative transition is needed.

cards.name: Lens Flare Transition
cards.what: A strong light point and optical rings cross the frame, cover the cut, and fade away.
cards.conveys: Suggests spatial travel through a camera and light.
useWhen: For cinematic openers or product reveals where light covers the cut
To convey movement in travel or sunrise scenes when the location changes

cards.name: Light Leak Transition
cards.what: A wide, irregular patch of colored light blooms across the frame, hides the cut, and fades.
cards.conveys: The heat and exposure marks of analog film: a warm, dreamy seam.
useWhen: Move between scenes in a film-like, memory, or travel-vlog tone.
When a warm overlay is needed to mask a cut.

sources.title: motion dictionary 2-transitions-camera.md#18. 라이트 리크 · Light Leak Transition

cards.name: Light Ray Transition
cards.what: Rays extend from a single point, cover the frame, and clear to the next scene.
cards.conveys: Conveys a strong reveal and spreading energy.
useWhen: Just before revealing a product or logo, to change scenes with an energy burst
To open a chapter with a strong entrance

cards.name: Luma Wipe
cards.what: Regions swap to the next scene in the brightness order of the footage itself or a grayscale helper image.
cards.conveys: Scenes open in whatever pattern or texture you choose: a classic broadcast transition.
useWhen: Open a scene in the shape of a logo, texture, or gradient.
Design an opening transition from a brand pattern.

cards.name: Luminance Melt
cards.what: Regions melt away upward or downward following the frame's brightness and noise, and the new scene takes over.
cards.conveys: The picture dissolves like a liquid, with bright areas running first.
useWhen: Subjects about time, decay, or change that melts away.
A directional, downward-flowing transition.

cards.name: Match on Action
cards.what: Objects or camera before and after a cut move in the same screen direction and speed flow, so two scenes read as one action.
cards.conveys: The cut goes unnoticed and the action carries through, making the transition feel like natural flow.
useWhen: A thrown object in scene A enters scene B from the same side.
Build continuity of action across different screens.

cards.name: Mirror Transition
cards.what: The video is mirrored or duplicated, folded to the center, then unfolded into the next video.
cards.conveys: Feels like space folds and connects to a different scene.
useWhen: For symmetric compositions or before-and-after videos where the frame folds to change
For intros themed around clones, symmetry, or mirrors

cards.name: Montage
cards.what: Several short images cut in succession, compressing a long process or theme.
cards.conveys: Conveys the passage of time, accumulation, or thematic connection.
useWhen: To compress a long span such as a build, growth, or daily routine into seconds
To show several benefits of a service in five short cuts

cards.name: Morph Match Cut
cards.what: A vermilion circle hard-cuts to a serif letter O at the same position and size, then the O morphs into a 62% donut chart.
cards.conveys: Three different scenes read as one idea because the shape carries across. The cut is crisp and the morph is smooth, so the flow never breaks.
useWhen: Use when moving from a concept scene to a data scene while keeping the same shape on screen.
Use when a logo, letter, and chart share a similar outline and should read as one continuous thought.

cards.name: Mosaic Traversal
cards.what: The footage spreads into cloned tiles, travels along the tile grid, and enters the new scene.
cards.conveys: A large move across a tiled world: the frame zooms out like a map and drops into another cell.
useWhen: Express a wide spatial move from one scene to a neighboring one.
When a zoom-out then zoom-in should relocate the view.

cards.name: Multiply Dissolve
cards.what: The two scenes multiply into a darker midpoint, then the brightness of the next scene returns.
cards.conveys: A weighty swap, dark and dense like a double exposure.
useWhen: Change scenes in a serious or heavy story.
When a white flash feels too light, use a dark counterpart.

cards.name: Noise Dissolve Transition
cards.what: Pixels whose noise value falls below the progress disappear first, so blotchy holes spread through the first scene and reveal the next.
cards.conveys: The outgoing scene melts away while the next one seeps through, marking the switch from question to answer softly but clearly.
useWhen: Move from a question scene to an answer or data scene.
Make a large switch from a dark cover plate to a light body plate.
Emphasize a scene change more than a plain crossfade would.

cards.name: Origami Fold Transition
cards.what: The scene folds into several panels and shrinks, and the new scene unfolds from the folded faces.
cards.conveys: Gives a 3D sense of folding and revealing a complex structure.
useWhen: To fold away complex content and unfold the next
For videos about origami, packaging, or brochures

cards.name: Outline Dissolve
cards.what: The scene loses its fill colors, leaving only bright outlines, then the new scene fills back in with color.
cards.conveys: Abstracts form so that two screens are bridged by shape.
useWhen: When changing content while keeping shape in diagram, blueprint, or icon-style videos
When a product photo turns into a line drawing and refills as another product

cards.name: Overlay Bridge
cards.what: The same foreground graphic sweeps across the scenes before and after a cut, tying them together.
cards.conveys: Keeps continuity between brand and scenes.
useWhen: When cutting the scene behind a logo or brand shape crossing the screen
When using a fixed overlay for section transitions in a series

cards.name: Paint Splatter Wipe
cards.what: Irregular paint blobs and dots spread and reveal the next scene.
cards.conveys: Adds a lively hand-splashed feel.
useWhen: To switch screens energetically in art, food, or casual brand tones
In creative tool or design service intros where color splashes are on-message

cards.name: Phosphor Trail Dissolve
cards.what: Trails of light from bright objects linger as the previous screen changes to the next.
cards.conveys: Evokes reverb and the memory of an electronic display.
useWhen: To keep screen afterglow in oscilloscope, radar, or CRT-themed videos
For sci-fi transitions where bright UI or text seems to persist

cards.name: Reaction Cut
cards.what: After an event or line, the view cuts to the face or reaction of someone who saw it.
cards.conveys: Confirms the emotion and impact of the event.
useWhen: When showing an audience or user reaction right after a surprising result in a talk, interview, or demo
When attaching another person's reaction after a statement in news or shorts to underline emotion

cards.name: Retreat and Cover
cards.what: The previous scene shrinks and darkens while the new scene slides in and covers it.
cards.conveys: Depth: the old scene retreats as the new topic steps forward.
useWhen: Tell a story where new content stacks on top like layers.
Keep the previous scene in memory while moving on.

cards.name: Ring Zoom
cards.what: Concentric rings show the footage at different magnifications, and the scene is replaced from the center.
cards.conveys: Tunnel-like layered focus and depth: the eye is pulled inward.
useWhen: Strongly gather attention on a central subject.
SF-style tunnel or warp looks.

cards.name: Scribble Wipe
cards.what: Scribble strokes stack up quickly to cover the frame, then wipe away to show the next scene.
cards.conveys: A rough, hand-drawn rhythm: a human touch that clean digital wipes lack.
useWhen: Change scenes in a hand-drawn, notebook, or sticker-styled video.
Hide a cut behind the covering moment.

cards.name: Shader Directional Warp Wipe
cards.what: A soft, bent diagonal edge sweeps across the frame while both plates near the edge stretch and smear along the direction of travel.
cards.conveys: Speed and physical drag as one scene is swept into the next, unlike a hard straight wipe.
useWhen: Cut from a sentence plate to a large-number plate with force.
Alternate light and dark scenes in sequence.
Add speed to a chapter-break transition.

sources.title: MDN, WebGL tutorial: Using textures in WebGL

cards.name: Shatter Transition
cards.what: The frame or object splits into small fragments that scatter and reveal the next scene; in reverse, fragments gather into the new scene.
cards.conveys: A strong impression of collapse and dispersal: the old scene falls apart like breaking glass.
useWhen: Convey the collapse of an old way or a shocking reversal.
Openers or climaxes that need a strong visual event.

cards.name: Shot Reverse Shot
cards.what: Opposite viewpoints of two speaking people alternate with speech and reaction.
cards.conveys: Makes the relationship and spatial continuity of a conversation clear.
useWhen: When switching the frame as the speaker changes in an interview or demo dialogue
In story-style videos where two characters trade questions and answers

cards.name: Smash Cut
cards.what: Two strongly contrasting scenes swap instantly without warning.
cards.conveys: Delivers shock, reversal, or a comic punchline.
useWhen: To reveal a messy outcome right after a grand plan and land the reversal
To jump from a quiet scene to a loud bright one for shock

sources.title: motion dictionary 2-transitions-camera.md#9. 스매시 컷 · Smash Cut

cards.name: Solarized Dissolve
cards.what: The scene passes through a high-contrast state with part of the colors and brightness inverted, then changes to the next scene.
cards.conveys: Creates an intense print-like effect and a strange jump between scenes.
useWhen: For surreal scene changes such as dreams, hallucination, or time jumps
For photographic print or experimental film-style music video cuts

cards.name: Speed Ramp
cards.what: Vary playback speed to slow down the peak of an action and accelerate surrounding movement.
cards.conveys: Concentrates attention on the action peak and changes rhythm.
useWhen: Spend more time on the peak of an action.
Accelerate repetitive parts of a product demonstration.

cards.name: J-cut and L-cut
cards.what: Sound changes before the picture (J-cut) or the old sound continues after the picture changes (L-cut).
cards.conveys: Announces the next scene early or holds the echo of the last. The cut flows smoothly.
useWhen: When narration starts the next scene's story before it appears
When an interview answer continues over cutaway footage

cards.name: Split Panel Handoff
cards.what: The title splits apart vertically and a panel grows from the opening to take over the screen.
cards.conveys: Focus hands off from words to a concrete screen, with the title acting as a door.
useWhen: Move from a title card into a real screen or demo.
Open a chapter title into body content.

cards.name: Static Band Wipe
cards.what: A horizontal noise band sweeps up or down, and everything behind it becomes the next scene.
cards.conveys: Gives an electronic sense of a scan replacing the screen.
useWhen: When switching screens in videos about monitors, surveillance cameras, or scans
For a directional wipe that signals order from top to bottom

cards.name: Swirl Transition
cards.what: The frame twists into a whirlpool around one point, then untwists on the next scene.
cards.conveys: Dimensional travel and a strong change of space: being pulled into another world.
useWhen: Move out of a scene or into a dream or another world in a story.
Express a big change of space in a single transition.

cards.name: Time Compression
cards.what: A long wait or repeated action is sped up or cut out so the piece jumps to the result, with a speed or ellipsis marker.
cards.conveys: Keeps the order of events while trimming dead time. Viewers know time has been compressed.
useWhen: When shortening waits on install, build or upload screens
When passing repeated input at 4x speed
When skipping the middle and jumping to the result screen

cards.name: Tinted Burn Dissolve
cards.what: The previous scene's color shifts to a hot tint as it blends into the next scene.
cards.conveys: A warm, temperature-laden move: covered in sunset or heat before the new scene emerges.
useWhen: Move between scenes with warm mood, such as heat, energy, or sunset.
When a color-tint swap is needed that is gentler than a burn.

cards.name: Translate Fade
cards.what: The old element moves off to the next position while fading, and the new one sharpens in the same travel zone.
cards.conveys: Combines lateral movement with a fading afterimage swap.
useWhen: When swapping card, tab, or slide content by sliding sideways
When replacing a text or number block with the next step naturally

cards.name: TV Static Transition
cards.what: Gray noise covers the screen briefly or blends with the scene before the next one appears.
cards.conveys: Evokes a channel change or signal loss.
useWhen: In news, retro, or horror tones when switching to another channel
To deliver a short signal drop as a scene-change jolt

cards.name: TV Tracking Transition
cards.what: Some horizontal scan lines wobble sideways, dark scan bars appear, and the scenes cross over.
cards.conveys: Creates the instability of old analog video.
useWhen: When a scene slips unstably in flashbacks, archival footage, or horror tones
When inserting analog artifacts between cuts in a VHS-look video

cards.name: Warp Dissolve
cards.what: The outgoing and incoming scenes bend and stretch in opposite directions as they swap, then the warp relaxes.
cards.conveys: Two states flow into each other like a morph.
useWhen: Make two scenes of similar shape or color feel connected.
Replace a flat crossfade at a chapter change.

cards.name: Wave Dissolve
cards.what: The whole frame bends and sways in periodic waves while the two scenes blend.
cards.conveys: A blurry, dreamlike boundary, as if seen through water.
useWhen: Enter dream, recollection, or imagined scenes.
When a full-frame wave is needed rather than a localized ripple.

cards.name: Wind Wipe
cards.what: The edge extends a different length on each line, like streaks blown by wind, to reveal the new scene.
cards.conveys: Speed and irregular flow: stripes sweep off in one direction.
useWhen: Scene moves that need speed.
Add texture when a straight wipe feels stiff.

cards.name: Zigzag Wipe
cards.what: Interlocking zigzag block boundaries move to reveal the new scene.
cards.conveys: Produces a dynamic, sawtooth progression.
useWhen: To swap scenes in sporty, techy, or street-style angular graphic videos
For directional wipes in list-style slide transitions

cards.name: Zoom Flash
cards.what: The frame zooms in fast and a bright flash carries it into the next scene at the peak.
cards.conveys: Sudden acceleration and impact locked to the beat: the speed of a hyperzoom.
useWhen: Change scenes on a strong beat.
Snap attention to a product or title.

cards.name: Zoom Wipe
cards.what: Mid-zoom on the center, a straight edge moves across the frame and reveals the new scene.
cards.conveys: The feeling of the camera pushing in while a page turns.
useWhen: Change scenes in videos with camera-move feel.
Add depth to a wipe.

cards.name: Text Cutout Zoom
cards.what: A scene shows through a letter-shaped hole, and the hole grows until it fills the frame.
cards.conveys: Feels like being pulled from the title into the next scene, joining title and scene into one flow.
useWhen: Move from a title card to the first scene of the main piece.
Open a chapter title into the next chapter footage.

cards.name: Text Half Split
cards.what: The top and bottom halves of a phrase split apart and a new phrase closes in from the opposite sides.
cards.conveys: Makes the swap moment crisp, giving replacement a clear stage-change rhythm.
useWhen: Replace one headline phrase with the next.
Emphasize the swap in a rotating keyword title.

cards.name: Title Card Rhythm
cards.what: Name or title cards appear on a steady beat and are quickly replaced.
cards.conveys: It sets information hierarchy and the rhythm of the piece; order tells what matters.
useWhen: Showing directing, production and cast names in sequence like film titles
Chaining chapter title cards on an even beat

cards.name: Ken Burns
cards.what: A camera move that slowly zooms into a still image while panning diagonally.
cards.conveys: Gives static material a flowing visual path and a calm sense of time.
useWhen: When presenting still photographs or printed illustrations in a video
When gradually guiding attention from the whole image to a specific detail

sources.title: motion dictionary 2-transitions-camera.md#24. 켄 번스 · Ken Burns Effect

cards.name: Pan
cards.what: A camera move that scans a wide scene in one direction while keeping the scale constant.
cards.conveys: Shows the sequence and flow of stages arranged across a space.
useWhen: When scanning a long process diagram in sequence
When stopping on the final subject in a horizontal scene

cards.name: Parallax
cards.what: A motion effect that creates depth by moving nearer layers faster and distant layers more slowly as the camera moves.
cards.conveys: Creates a sense of distance and space between flat elements.
useWhen: When showing the distance between foreground and background
When moving elements at multiple depths in a scrolling scene

cards.name: Push-in
cards.what: A camera move that slowly approaches a fixed focal point in a sentence or scene.
cards.conveys: Increases the emphasis on and attention to a key word.
useWhen: When focusing on a key word after showing the full sentence
When showing an important part of a product or subject up close

cards.name: Rack Focus
cards.what: A focus shift that swaps sharpness between foreground and background subjects without changing their positions.
cards.conveys: Shifts visual priority from the foreground subject to the background subject.
useWhen: When transferring attention between foreground and background
When changing the relative emphasis of two subjects without moving the scene

sources.title: motion dictionary 2-transitions-camera.md#25. 랙 포커스 · Rack Focus / Focus Pull

cards.name: Zoom to Detail
cards.what: A motion that centers and enlarges a specific coordinate in an overview diagram to reveal detail.
cards.conveys: Moves into a detailed explanation while preserving the relationship between the whole and its parts.
useWhen: When showing details of one subject within a node diagram or map
When explaining a selected point after showing the overall structure
